In networks, sparsity means that most possible pairs of nodes are not connected, so adjacency matrices are mostly zeros. Sparse, high-dimensional representations are inefficient to store and compute with, and they give machine learning models little signal about how nodes relate, especially for nodes with few connections. DeepWalk (Perozzi et al., 2014) addresses this by running truncated random walks over the graph to generate node sequences, then applying the skip-gram model from word2vec to those sequences. This learns dense, low-dimensional vector embeddings in which nodes with similar neighborhoods or structural roles have similar vectors. These embeddings can then be used as features for standard machine learning tasks such as node classification, link prediction, and visualization.
